correctness.rationale: Necessity: if both cliques begin with two white vertices, no blue vertex can force, so a one-leak set requires a full or nearly-full layer. For n>=4 and layer A missing i, the available initial A forcers are precisely a_j at selected B indices j!=i; one leak can suppress all if <=1 such j, and B cannot initiate while there are >=2 white B. With >=2 such indices a non-leaked A forcer completes A; thereafter cross-layer forces all B except perhaps one, completed within B. Full layer is always forcing even with one A leak. n=3 gives additional precisely 9 two-and-two configurations. Counting disjoint full-layer configurations and the two near-full orientations, with the both-near-full overlap n^2 counted once, gives exactly L_n=2z^n(1+z)^n-z^(2n)+2n*C(n-1,2)z^(n+1)+2n*sum_{t=3}^{n-2}C(n,t)z^(n-1+t)+n^2 z^(2n-2) for n>=4; L3=2z^3+15z^4+6z^5+z^6. Minimal sets are exactly two full layers and 2n*C(n-1,2) near-full plus two sets for n>=4, or two layers plus nine 4-sets for n=3. Independently exhaustive bit-mask sequential-forcing closure with every leak and all subsets for n=3,4,5,6 matched both polynomials and inclusion-minimal histograms. This is finite corroboration; case argument proves all n.
